rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 5 'Design principles' (lines 119-125): all 7 numbered items bold a full lead SENTENCE, not a sub-span handle — e.g. line 119 '**A skill never duplicates another's logic.**' (subject+verb+object, 6 words) and line 123 '**The loop is re-invocation, not internal recursion.**' (7 words, full clause). This is a law/consolidation slide, so 'one handle per law' is allowed by the exception clause, but the bolded spans here are the entire lead sentences, which §9 explicitly bans regardless of the per-law count ('never a whole lead sentence') — this is the canonical pre-2026-07-09 monoculture the rule names as its violation shape. Even under the supplementary-page lookup-surface waiver, the waiver requires 'bold the label, not the sentence after it', and there is no separate label here — the whole sentence is bolded. Secondary, weaker evidence in chunk 7 line 154-159: 3 of 5 'What's special' bullets bold a full verb-bearing clause ('**`/ship` is the only orchestrator.**', '**`/aios` is pure routing.**', '**Mandatory gates fire positionally.**') rather than a noun-phrase handle, while the other 2 bullets ('**Front-loaded read-only analysis.**', '**Re-invocation as control flow.**') are correctly label-shaped noun phrases.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Chunk 5: trim each bold to a short handle noun-phrase (e.g. bold only 'No duplication.' or the coined term, move the rest to plain lead prose). Chunk 7: same trim for the 3 sentence-shaped bolds; the 2 label-shaped ones are fine as-is.
